That matches what I expected. As I typed "creamy" the list narrowed on the fly, and it kept the roast-potato bookmark even though "creamy" is only in its little description, not the title — so search is looking past just the titles, which is the whole point for me when I only half-remember something. And it's good to know it's also checking the site name, address, and labels, since sometimes the word I remember is the label I gave it.

A few things about searching that matter to me in real use — I want to make sure they hold up before I call search done:

- If I type in a different case — say "CREAMY" or "Creamy" — I'd still expect the same result. It shouldn't care about capital letters.
- Sometimes I want to search specifically by a label rather than have it mixed in with words in the text — like a quick way to say "just show me things tagged recipes."
- When I remember an exact phrase — a few words in a row — I'd want to search for that exact wording and not have it match items that just happen to contain those words scattered around.
- And when I have a lot saved, being able to combine things — like "potatoes but not the carrot one," or "recipes or work" — so I can narrow down instead of scrolling.

Can you show me how searching handles those?
